alice-springs-1.name: Alice Springs Desert Park
alice-springs-1.bio: Desert wildlife park with a nocturnal house, free-flying bird shows and Aboriginal-guided talks, seven kilometres from town.

alice-springs-2.name: Alice Springs Telegraph Station
alice-springs-2.bio: Best-preserved stop on the 1872 Overland Telegraph Line, with restored stone buildings, a post office and walking trails.
alice-springs-2.hours: Reserve 8:00 AM – 9:00 PM; heritage precinct to 4:00 PM

alice-springs-3.name: Araluen Cultural Precinct
alice-springs-3.bio: Arts centre galleries, the Central Australian Aviation Museum and Central Craft, in a precinct two kilometres west of town.
alice-springs-3.hours: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM daily Mar–Oct; closed Mondays Nov–Feb

alice-springs-4.name: Anzac Hill
alice-springs-4.bio: Hilltop war memorial and lookout over Alice Springs and the MacDonnell Ranges, a short walk or drive from town.

alice-springs-5.name: Emily Gap
alice-springs-5.bio: Sacred Arrernte gap east of town with a rock painting of the caterpillar dreaming, reached by a short walk.

alice-springs-6.name: Royal Flying Doctor Service Tourist Facility
alice-springs-6.bio: Original 1939 flying doctor base with a John Flynn hologram, virtual-reality flight and museum.

alice-springs-7.name: Old Ghan Heritage Railway and Museum
alice-springs-7.bio: Museum about the original Ghan railway, with a steam engine and historic carriages parked outside.
alice-springs-7.wiki: Old Ghan Heritage Railway and Museum

alice-springs-8.name: Olive Pink Botanic Garden
alice-springs-8.bio: Free arid-zone botanic garden with over 600 plant species, bushfood trails and a hill lookout over town.

alice-springs-9.name: Women's Museum of Australia
alice-springs-9.bio: Museum of Australian women's achievements, housed in the Old Gaol, whose buildings are included in the ticket.
alice-springs-9.hours: Tue–Sat 10:00 AM – 3:00 PM; doors close 2:30 PM

alice-springs-10.name: Adelaide House
alice-springs-10.bio: 1926 stone hospital designed by John Flynn, now a small museum with a guided tour and tea.
alice-springs-10.hours: Mon, Tue, Thu and market Sundays 10:00 AM – 1:00 PM

alice-springs-11.name: Alice Springs Reptile Centre
alice-springs-11.bio: Over 100 reptiles in recreated habitats, with a saltwater crocodile viewed from underground and daily talks.

alice-springs-12.name: National Road Transport Museum
alice-springs-12.bio: Halls of vintage trucks, including Bertha, Australia's first road train, plus classic cars and a Wall of Fame.

east-macdonnell-ranges-1.name: Trephina Gorge Nature Park
east-macdonnell-ranges-1.bio: Quartzite gorge lined with river red gums, with short walks, waterholes and the largest ghost gum in Central Australia.

east-macdonnell-ranges-2.name: Arltunga Historical Reserve
east-macdonnell-ranges-2.bio: Central Australia's first town, a gold-rush site 110 km east of Alice Springs, with restored stone buildings.
east-macdonnell-ranges-2.hours: Reserve 24 hours; visitor centre 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM

east-macdonnell-ranges-3.name: Corroboree Rock
east-macdonnell-ranges-3.bio: Dark grey dolomite column sacred to the Eastern Arrernte, with a short walk around its base off the Ross Highway.

east-macdonnell-ranges-4.name: N'Dhala Gorge Nature Park
east-macdonnell-ranges-4.bio: Gorge protecting about 6,000 rock engravings along a 1.5 km walking track, reached only by 4WD.

west-macdonnell-national-park-1.name: Ormiston Gorge
west-macdonnell-national-park-1.bio: Red-walled gorge with a deep permanent waterhole about 500 m from the visitor centre and the Ormiston Pound circuit.

west-macdonnell-national-park-6.name: Larapinta Trail
west-macdonnell-national-park-6.bio: Walking trail of about 230 km in 12 sections along the West MacDonnell Ranges from Alice Springs to Mount Sonder.
west-macdonnell-national-park-6.hours: Open year-round; book multi-day walking and campsites online

west-macdonnell-national-park-2.name: Standley Chasm
west-macdonnell-national-park-2.bio: Sheer-walled red chasm on Arrernte land, reached by a 2.4 km round-trip path; also called Angkerle Atwatye.
west-macdonnell-national-park-2.hours: Mon-Sat 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM; Sun 8:00 AM - 2:00 PM

west-macdonnell-national-park-3.name: Simpsons Gap
west-macdonnell-national-park-3.bio: Gap in the ranges 18 km west of Alice Springs, with a waterhole, rock-wallaby habitat and a walking track.

west-macdonnell-national-park-4.name: Ellery Creek Big Hole
west-macdonnell-national-park-4.bio: Permanent waterhole beneath red cliffs, a five-minute walk from the car park, known for cold swimming and camping.

west-macdonnell-national-park-5.name: Glen Helen Gorge
west-macdonnell-national-park-5.bio: Gorge and waterhole a short stroll from the car park, used for swimming and as a lunch stop beside the Glen Helen resort.

west-macdonnell-national-park-7.name: Mount Sonder
west-macdonnell-national-park-7.bio: Grade 4 summit walk to the 1,379 m peak at the Larapinta Trail's western end, with views over the ranges.
west-macdonnell-national-park-7.hours: Open daily; start early, little shade

west-macdonnell-national-park-8.name: Serpentine Gorge
west-macdonnell-national-park-8.bio: Narrow gorge about 100 km west of Alice Springs, with a short walk through to Inarlanga Pass.

west-macdonnell-national-park-9.name: Ochre Pits
west-macdonnell-national-park-9.bio: Coloured ochre quarry faces that Arrernte people have mined for generations, with a short walk from the car park.

west-macdonnell-national-park-10.name: Redbank Gorge
west-macdonnell-national-park-10.bio: Narrow chasm and cold swimming hole at the foot of Mount Sonder, reached by a short walk from the car park.

watarrka-national-park-1.name: Kings Canyon
watarrka-national-park-1.bio: Sandstone canyon with walls up to 270 m high, seen from the Rim Walk or the creek-bed walk below.
watarrka-national-park-1.hours: Open daily; Rim Walk start before 9 AM on days forecast 36°C or higher

watarrka-national-park-2.name: Kings Canyon Rim Walk
watarrka-national-park-2.bio: Grade 4 loop of 6 km over the canyon rim, past the Garden of Eden waterhole; allow three to four hours.
watarrka-national-park-2.hours: Open daily; start before 9 AM on days forecast 36°C or higher

watarrka-national-park-3.name: Kings Creek Walk
watarrka-national-park-3.bio: Easy 2 km return walk along Kings Creek at the foot of the canyon, a short alternative to the Rim Walk.

watarrka-national-park-4.name: Kathleen Springs Walk
watarrka-national-park-4.bio: Paved, wheelchair-accessible 2.4 km return walk to a spring-fed waterhole at the head of Kathleen Gorge.

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-1.name: Uluru
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-1.bio: Sandstone monolith sacred to Anangu, with a 9.8 km base walk and sunrise and sunset viewing areas.
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-1.hours: Park hours by month: 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (Dec–Feb) to 6:30 AM – 7:30 PM (Jun–Jul)

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-2.name: Kata Tjuta
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-2.bio: Group of 36 domed rock formations west of Uluru, sacred to Anangu, with walks through its gorges.
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-2.hours: Park hours by month: 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (Dec–Feb) to 6:30 AM – 7:30 PM (Jun–Jul); leave 45 min before closing

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-3.name: Uluru Base Walk
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-3.bio: Flat 9.8 km track around the base of Uluru, taking three to four hours, with sacred sites marked by signs.
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-3.hours: Park hours by month: 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (Dec–Feb) to 6:30 AM – 7:30 PM (Jun–Jul)

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-4.name: Valley of the Winds Walk
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-4.bio: Grade 4 circuit of about 7.4 km among the Kata Tjuta domes to two lookouts, taking three to four hours.
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-4.hours: Park hours; closes at Karu Lookout from 11 AM when 36°C or more is forecast

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-5.name: Uluru-Kata Tjuta Cultural Centre
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-5.bio: Visitor and cultural centre near the base of Uluru, with Anangu art, galleries, exhibitions and a café.

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-6.name: Field of Light
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-6.bio: Bruce Munro's light installation of illuminated stems near Yulara, seen at sunrise or after dark.
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-6.hours: Sunrise and after-dark sessions (times vary by season)

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-7.name: Talinguru Nyakunytjaku
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-7.bio: Sunrise viewing area for Uluru and Kata Tjuta, with platforms and a 1.4 km circuit of two short walks.
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-7.hours: Park hours by month: 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (Dec–Feb) to 6:30 AM – 7:30 PM (Jun–Jul)

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-8.name: Mala Walk
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-8.bio: Easy 2 km return walk from the Mala car park along Uluru's base to Kantju Gorge, with a daily ranger walk.
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-8.hours: Park hours by month: 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (Dec–Feb) to 6:30 AM – 7:30 PM (Jun–Jul); ranger walk 8 AM (Oct–Apr), 10 AM (May–Sep)

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-9.name: Kuniya Walk
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-9.bio: One-kilometre return walk to Mutitjulu Waterhole on Uluru's south side, with rock art and a creation story.
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-9.hours: Park hours by month: 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (Dec–Feb) to 6:30 AM – 7:30 PM (Jun–Jul)

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-10.name: Walpa Gorge Walk
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-10.bio: Easy 2.6 km return walk into a gorge between two Kata Tjuta domes, with steep rock walls either side.
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-10.hours: Park hours by month: 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (Dec–Feb) to 6:30 AM – 7:30 PM (Jun–Jul)

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-11.name: Yulara
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-11.bio: Resort village just outside the park, the base for accommodation, dining, tours and flights to Uluru.

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-12.name: Imalung Lookout
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-12.bio: Sand-dune lookout on the Yulara drive loop with views of Uluru and part of Kata Tjuta.

uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-13.name: Kata Tjuta Dune Viewing Area
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-13.bio: Short walk up a sand dune beside the Kata Tjuta road, with views of the domes and Uluru in the distance.
uluru-kata-tjuta-national-park-13.hours: Park hours by month: 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (Dec–Feb) to 6:30 AM – 7:30 PM (Jun–Jul)

finke-gorge-national-park.name: Finke Gorge National Park
finke-gorge-national-park.bio: Remote national park around the Finke River and Palm Valley, reached by high-clearance 4WD along the river bed.
finke-gorge-national-park.hours: Open 24 hours; road may close after rain

palm-valley.name: Palm Valley
palm-valley.bio: Oasis of rare red cabbage palms and cycads, with short walks and a lookout over Palm Creek.
palm-valley.hours: Open 24 hours; road may close after rain

gosses-bluff.name: Gosses Bluff (Tnorala)
gosses-bluff.bio: Ring of hills left by a meteorite impact, sacred ground on the Mereenie Loop road, reached by 4WD.

chambers-pillar.name: Chambers Pillar
chambers-pillar.bio: A 50 m sandstone column rising from the desert plain, reached by a 4WD track south of Alice Springs, best at sunset.
chambers-pillar.hours: Open 24 hours; road may close after rain

rainbow-valley.name: Rainbow Valley
rainbow-valley.bio: Reserve of striped sandstone bluffs and cliffs south of Alice Springs, with short walks to the claypan.

ewaninga-conservation-reserve.name: Ewaninga Rock Carvings
ewaninga-conservation-reserve.bio: Small reserve of ancient rock engravings on a sandstone outcrop, south of Alice Springs on the Old South Road.
ewaninga-conservation-reserve.wiki: Napwerte / Ewaninga Rock Carvings Conservation Reserve

henbury-meteorites-conservation-reserve.name: Henbury Meteorites
henbury-meteorites-conservation-reserve.bio: Twelve small craters formed by a meteorite impact about 4,700 years ago, with short walks around them.

curtin-springs.name: Curtin Springs
curtin-springs.bio: Family-run cattle station and roadside inn on the Lasseter Highway with camping, a store and meals, on the way to Uluru.

held.hermannsburg: Historic Precinct closed for the 2026 season
